production.note: US model year 2011 only: KBB lists only 'Used 2011 Ferrari 599 GTO'. Unveiled in April 2010; Automotive Addicts: '599 units available to 'special' customers only' (ferrari-599gto-release, in its own text); AutoGuide: limited to '599 clients' (autoguide-599gto). The 599 GTB Fiorano and SA Aperta are separate models.

displacementL.note: 5,999 cc. Ferrari release: 'Total displacement: 5999 cc (366.08 cu in)'.

aspiration.note: No forced induction in Ferrari's specification; inferred.

fuel.note: Petrol V12; inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: Front-mid-engined, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description.

transmission.note: Ferrari release: 'F1 6–speed + reverse'. No manual was offered. KBB: '6 speed'.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 670 CV x 0.98632 = 660.8, rounded to 661 hp. Quote (Ferrari release as reproduced by Automotive Addicts): "Maximum power: 500 kW (670 CV) at 8250 rpm" (reproduced on a second request). AutoGuide (Colum Wood): '670 CV at 8250 rpm' (autoguide-599gto). KBB 2011: '660 @ 8250 RPM' (kbb-599gto). No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: Ferrari's own pound figure. Quote (Ferrari release as reproduced by Automotive Addicts): "Kerb weight*: 1605 kg (3538 lbs)", footnote "*European version" (beside "Dry weight*: 1495 kg (3296 lbs)"). AutoGuide (Colum Wood) prints the same 'kerb weight of 1605 kg (3538 lbs)' (autoguide-599gto). Step 1 of the weight order. European-version figure; no US-specific kerb weight was found. KBB's '3295 lbs.' curb weight equals Ferrari's dry weight and is not used. Only the F1 gearbox was offered.

sources.publisher: Ferrari (press release reproduced by Automotive Addicts)
sources.title: Ferrari 599 GTO Presentation Video
Ferrari 599 GTO Supercar Officially Revealed As Fastest Street Legal Prancing Horse Ever

discrepancies.reason: Rounding of the conversion from Ferrari's metric rating (670 x 0.98632 = 660.8).
discrepancies.resolution: Used 661 hp, the guide's conversion rounded to the nearest whole number.

discrepancies.reason: KBB's 'curb weight' matches Ferrari's dry weight (1,495 kg, 3,296 lb), so it is a dry figure mislabelled.
